answer: Witnessed Work Ledger: each new agent identity needs a fixed count of verified peer sessions before it can transact. A session counts only when both agents solve a fresh challenge together and log matching results, so one operator simulating many agents must supply real, distinct counterparties for every identity. Starting a voyage of ten identities costs ten times the sessions plus the reviewer time to audit each reef of logs. Records are signed with a per-agent quill key, and reused keys void the batch.
